title: POV: Your Mornings Save YOU $3,276 a Year — Jake Spends $14 Before 9 AM Every Day
description:
A simple morning routine that makes you more productive and saves money: same job, same paycheck, but your mornings are worth about $3,276 a year more than Jake's.

In this POV story, Jake hits snooze three times, wakes up at 8:50 and buys a $6 latte and an $8 breakfast sandwich on the way to work, every workday: about $3,528 a year. You prepare in 10 minutes the night before, charge your phone across the room, skip the phone for the first 30 minutes, walk for 10 minutes, eat a $1 breakfast at home, do a 10-minute money check (balance, yesterday's charges, bills due this week) and pick your top 3 tasks, hardest first.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 Two Mornings
0:57 The Night Before
2:14 The Snooze Trap
2:51 The $14 Morning
3:58 Your First 30 Minutes
5:36 The Money Check
6:53 Your Top 3
7:44 The Math
8:15 One Year Later

💬 What's the first thing you do in the morning? Be honest: is it your phone? Tell me in the comments!
👍 Subscribe to Simple Money Life for a new simple money move every day.

Numbers are an example: $14 a day × about 252 workdays = $3,528 a year vs about $1 a day at home ($252); your own costs will differ.

⚠️ This video is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice.

🎵 Music: original background track

short2.title: POV: You Wait 24 Hours Before Buying… and Keep $1,140 a Year 🛒
short2.description: The 24-hour rule: when you want something you didn't plan to buy, put it in the cart, close the app and wait one day. Most late-night wants are gone by morning. Skip just $95 a month of impulse buys and that's $1,140 a year.
